## Core Overview
- Primary purpose: Provide foundational statistical knowledge tailored for 5th semester Artificial Intelligence (FA24-BAI) students.
- Fundamental themes: Probability distributions, statistical inference, data analysis, and measuring uncertainty in AI models.

## Key Concepts & Formulas
- Expected Value: E[X] = sum(x * P(x)) for discrete variables, representing the long-run average outcome.
- Variance and Standard Deviation: Var(X) = E[(X - E[X])^2] = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2, measuring the dispersion of a distribution.
- Conditional Probability: P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B), essential for Bayesian inference and classification algorithms.
- Bayes Theorem: P(A | B) = [P(B | A) * P(A)] / P(B), foundational for Naive Bayes classifiers.
- Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE): Method of estimating parameters of a probability distribution by maximizing a likelihood function.
- Central Limit Theorem: The sampling distribution of the mean approaches a normal distribution as sample size n increases, regardless of the population distribution.

## Exam Takeaways
- Master the derivation and application of Bayes Theorem for classification tasks.
- Understand how to calculate mean, variance, and standard deviation for both discrete and continuous random variables.
- Know the difference between population parameters and sample statistics.
- Be prepared to solve problems involving probability density functions (PDF) and cumulative distribution functions (CDF).
- Expect questions linking statistical variance directly to overfitting and model uncertainty in machine learning contexts.
